pois.name: Main Parking & Trailhead
pois.description: Free gravel parking lot at 3 Old Country Rd and main starting hub for all Refuge trails.
pois.kidTip: Start and end your walk here — check the trailhead board for seasonal bird sightings!

pois.name: Outdoor Wildlife Complex
pois.description: Home to permanently injured native New York wildlife ambassadors including owls, hawks, falcons, and foxes.
pois.kidTip: Look quietly into the tall aviaries to spot barred owls, screech owls, and red-tailed hawks.

pois.name: Charles Banks Belt Nature Center
pois.description: Historic lakeside Nature Center overlooking Old Ice Pond (undergoing renovation & expansion).
pois.kidTip: Peek out over Old Ice Pond right beside the building to look for painted turtles and ducks.

pois.name: Outdoor Restrooms
pois.description: Accessible outdoor restrooms open daily from sunrise to sunset near the Butterfly Garden.
pois.kidTip: Good pit stop right at the start or end of your walk!

pois.name: Butterfly Garden & Greenhouse
pois.description: Native Long Island pollinator garden and greenhouse where resident giant tortoises live.
pois.kidTip: Look for monarch butterflies on goldenrod and milkweed in warm months, plus giant tortoises in the greenhouse!

pois.name: Woodland Amphitheater
pois.description: Shaded outdoor wooden seating area along the east trail used for nature talks and school groups.
pois.kidTip: Take a quick rest on the curved benches and listen for woodpeckers tapping nearby.

pois.name: Ice Harvesting Exhibit & Bog
pois.description: Scenic wooden boardwalk over the southern bog showcasing how the Quogue Ice Company harvested pond ice in the 1910s.
pois.kidTip: Before freezers existed, people sawed giant blocks of winter ice right out of Old Ice Pond!

pois.name: Old Ice Pond
pois.description: 10-acre freshwater pond dotted with mossy islands — a favorite sanctuary for waterfowl, turtles, and osprey.
pois.kidTip: Count how many tiny wooded islands you can spot floating across the pond.

pois.name: The Bridge
pois.description: Wooden footbridge spanning the lush wetland channel connecting the northern swamp into Old Ice Pond.
pois.kidTip: Pause in the middle of the bridge and look straight down into the water for frogs and dragonflies.

pois.name: Eastern Bluebird Nestboxes (New Trail)
pois.description: Open Forest Regeneration Area along the New Trail featuring wooden nestboxes for bright blue Eastern Bluebirds.
pois.kidTip: Look for tiny wooden birdhouses mounted on posts in the sunny clearing — bluebirds love open meadows!

pois.name: North Pond
pois.description: Quiet freshwater marsh pond tucked between pine-oak woodland and swamp — great for spotting herons and wood ducks.
pois.kidTip: Whisper softly as you walk up to the shore so you don’t spook resting ducks or turtles.

pois.name: Deer Pond Overlook
pois.description: Tranquil northern forest pond with a wooden waterside bench where white-tailed deer often come to drink.
pois.kidTip: Check the soft sandy trail near the bench for heart-shaped deer hoofprints!

pois.name: Dwarf Pine Barrens
pois.description: One of the rarest ecosystems in the world — ancient pitch pines that naturally grow only 4 to 8 feet tall.
pois.kidTip: Even though these miniature pine trees are shorter than a basketball hoop, some are over 50 years old!

pois.name: Fairy Dell Boardwalk
pois.description: Elevated wooden catwalk south of the railroad tracks winding through tidal wetlands along Quantuck Creek.
pois.kidTip: Walk carefully across Old Country Rd to reach the boardwalk — watch for fiddler crabs and egrets from the platforms!
